title: Regularity ascends along smooth ring maps
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and assume $R$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (Noetherian, with every localization at a prime ideal a regular local ring). Then $S$ is a regular ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NF (lemma-regular-goes-up, line 49772) and its proof (Lemma Tag 033A lemma-Rk-goes-up applied for all (R_k), with Lemma Tag 00TT lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field)

proof.text: Because $R$ is regular, it is Noetherian. The smooth presentation in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] makes $S$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra, so $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence, line 5991), applied to the finite-presentation clause of smoothness

proof.text: The map $R\to S$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat], the flatness assertion in the smooth-ring-map overview used by the proof of 07NF.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic, line 37438) and the smooth-ring-map overview

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the fibre $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finite-type smooth algebra over the residue field, and every localization of that fibre at a prime is a regular local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-fibre-regular-local]. Thus each fibre has property $(R_k)$ for every integer $k\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00T4 (lemma-base-change-smooth, line 37133), the smooth-ring-map overview, and Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 41349)

proof.text: For every integer $k\ge0$, $R$ has property $(R_k)$ because every localization of the regular ring $R$ at a prime is regular local. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-regularity-rk-goes-up] to the Noetherian rings $R,S$, the flat map from Step 2, the fibre property from Step 3, and the property for $R$, gives property $(R_k)$ for $S$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NF (lemma-regular-goes-up, line 49772), by applying Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up, line 49612) for every k

proof.text: Since $S$ is Noetherian and has property $(R_k)$ for every $k$, every localization $S_{\mathfrak q}$ at a prime is regular local. Hence $S$ is a regular ring by [def-weil-regular-scheme].
